demand.question: What is AWS WAF in one sentence: a web application firewall that watches HTTP(S) requests to a protected resource and allows, blocks or counts them by rules?

Which resource types can a protection pack (web ACL) protect today: CloudFront distributions, Application Load Balancers, API Gateway REST APIs, AppSync GraphQL APIs, Cognito user pools, App Runner services, Verified Access instances, Amplify apps (list exactly what the page lists)?
demand.note: register-08 added waf-protected-resource-types from the web-acl page sentence (the what-is list cannot be quoted line by line).

demand.question: Which resources can AWS WAF NOT be attached to that exam options offer (Network Load Balancer, EC2 instance directly, API Gateway HTTP API, Global Accelerator)? Ground each 'cannot' in a page sentence, or record it as unsupported and drop it.
demand.note: No saved page has a cannot-sentence for NLB, EC2, API Gateway HTTP API or Global Accelerator (searched what-is-aws-waf, how-aws-waf-works-resources, web-acl, web-acl-associating-aws-resource, WAF FAQ). Teach these as not in the supported list (waf-protected-resource-types); only ALB on Outposts has a quoted cannot.

demand.question: What is the scope difference between a global (CloudFront) protection pack and a Regional one, and in which Region must a CloudFront protection pack be created or managed (US East (N. Virginia))?

How many protection packs (web ACLs) can one resource be associated with at a time, and can one web ACL protect many resources? What is the quota on ALB associations per web ACL (changed 2025-10-22 and 2026-05-01)?
Can AWS WAF protect a website that is not hosted in AWS (through a CloudFront distribution with a custom origin)?
When an ALB sits behind CloudFront, where does the web ACL go, and how do you stop clients from bypassing CloudFront to reach the ALB directly?
demand.note: Cookie forwarding for the token is grounded; how to stop clients bypassing CloudFront to reach the ALB is a CloudFront topic (custom origin header or managed prefix list): no saved WAF page; search for bypass found nothing in WAF pages. Leave to the CloudFront chapter.

demand.question: How does a protection pack evaluate a request: rules in priority order, the first terminating action stops evaluation, and the default action (Allow or Block) applies when no rule matches?
Which rule actions exist (Allow, Block, Count, CAPTCHA, Challenge), which are terminating, and what does Count do (match, label, keep evaluating) for safe testing of a new rule?
Which rule statement detects SQL injection, and what does the sensitivity level option (added 2022-07) change?
Which rule statement detects cross-site scripting (XSS), and which request parts can it inspect?
What does a geographic match statement do (block or allow by country; Region-level granularity added 2022-11; adds labels), and how is it different from CloudFront geographic restrictions?
demand.note: Geo match behaviour grounded; the comparison with CloudFront geographic restrictions belongs to the CloudFront chapter.

demand.question: How do you block a list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges in AWS WAF (IP set match; IPv4 and IPv6 sets)?
What is the maximum number of IP addresses or ranges in one IP set, and how many IP sets per account per Region?
What do the ASN match (2025-06), size constraint, string match and regex match statements inspect, in one line each?

How much of a request body does AWS WAF inspect by default for each resource type (ALB and AppSync vs CloudFront, API Gateway, Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access), and what is the largest configurable limit (changed 2023-04-11 and 2024-03-07)?
What does AWS WAF do with the part of a body (or headers, cookies) beyond the inspection limit (oversize handling: continue, match, no match)?
How does AWS WAF find the real client IP behind a proxy or CDN (forwarded IP configuration, X-Forwarded-For)?

What does a rate-based rule do: count requests per aggregation key over an evaluation window and apply its action to keys over the limit; which aggregation keys exist (source IP, forwarded IP, header, URI path, ASN, JA3/JA4, custom keys)?
What is the lowest rate limit a rate-based rule accepts today, and what was it before 2024-08-30?
Which evaluation windows can a rate-based rule use (configurable since 2024-02-28), and what was the only window before?
Rate-based rule caveats: is the count exact, and how quickly does WAF start and stop limiting a key?
How do you rate-limit only one part of a site, such as the login page (scope-down statement), and can you exempt trusted IP ranges?
Why does a rate-based rule stop a distributed attack from many IP addresses better than a static IP block list (Callvale: 60,000 attempts from 1,400 addresses)?
What are web ACL capacity units (WCUs), what is the maximum WCU per protection pack and per rule group, and above how many WCUs is extra cost charged (changed 2023-04-11)?
Other AWS WAF quotas the exam can touch: web ACLs per account per Region, rule groups, regex pattern sets, rules per rule group, geo match countries per rule (quota added 2025-08-29).
What are managed rule groups: AWS Managed Rules (free for most) vs AWS Marketplace seller rule groups (subscription)? Which AWS Managed Rules groups need an extra fee?
What do the baseline AWS Managed Rules groups cover (core rule set and OWASP-style risks, known bad inputs, admin protection), and the use-case groups (SQL database, Linux, PHP, WordPress)?
What do the Amazon IP reputation list and the Anonymous IP list rule groups block?
What is AWS WAF Bot Control (common vs targeted inspection levels), and is it charged on top of the protection pack?

What does Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP) protect (login page, stolen credentials, credential stuffing), and how is it different from Bot Control and from account creation fraud prevention (ACFP)?
What do the CAPTCHA and Challenge actions do, how do tokens work, and when is each the right action?
What is the AWS WAF Anti-DDoS managed rule group / application layer (L7) DDoS protection (2025-06), and what is resource-level DDoS protection for ALB?
Can a blocked request get a custom response (status code, body, headers), and can WAF insert custom headers into allowed requests?
Where can AWS WAF send full request logs (CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, Amazon Data Firehose), and how many destinations per protection pack?
demand.note: Destinations grounded; no saved page states how many destinations one web ACL can have (searched logging, logging-destinations, logging-management-configure for destination per / one logging destination).

demand.question: AWS WAF pricing dimensions: per protection pack per month, per rule per month, per million requests, extra for Bot Control / Fraud Control / CAPTCHA, extra WCU above the included amount.
demand.note: The price tables on www/waf/pricing are not in the snapshot (rendered by script); only the worked examples carry rates. The CAPTCHA rate ($0.40 per thousand attempts) appears only in the Case G example as the 6th line under its heading, outside the heading-scoped evidence window; Bot Control per-request rates appear only inside examples.

demand.question: What is AWS Shield Standard: automatic, no extra charge, for every AWS customer; which attack types and layers does it protect against (network and transport layer, for example SYN floods and UDP reflection)?

What does AWS Shield Advanced add over Standard: enhanced detection, Shield Response Team, DDoS cost protection, automatic application layer mitigation, health-based detection, visibility and reports?
Which resource types can Shield Advanced protect (CloudFront, Route 53 hosted zones, Global Accelerator, ALB, Elastic IP addresses for EC2 and NLB)?
What does Shield Advanced cost (monthly subscription fee, commitment term, data transfer out usage fees), and does one fee cover all accounts in an organization?
Does Shield Advanced include AWS WAF (and Firewall Manager) usage for protected resources at no extra cost?
What is DDoS cost protection: credits for scaling charges caused by a DDoS attack on protected resources; how is a credit requested?
Who can contact the Shield Response Team (SRT), which AWS Support plan is required, and what can the SRT do in your account?
What is proactive engagement, and what must be configured for it (Route 53 health checks on protected resources, contacts)?
How does Shield Advanced automatic application layer DDoS mitigation work: it needs a web ACL on the resource and manages rules in a Shield rule group (Count or Block)?
What are Shield Advanced protection groups, and what does health-based detection add?
Shield Advanced quotas that the exam can touch (protections, protection groups).
What are the common DDoS attack types by layer (UDP reflection, SYN flood at layers 3 and 4; HTTP floods, cache-busting at layer 7)?
What does a DDoS-resilient architecture look like (CloudFront and Route 53 at the edge, Global Accelerator, ELB, Auto Scaling, reduce the attack surface, security groups and NACLs)?
Can AWS Shield protect resources that run outside AWS (on premises), and how (CloudFront or Global Accelerator in front)?
demand.note: CloudFront with a custom origin is grounded (shield-protect-sites-outside-aws-via-cloudfront, shield-faq-protect-outside-lock-down-backend names CloudFront or Route 53); no Shield page names Global Accelerator for this case.

demand.question: How quickly does Shield detect and mitigate events, and how fast is an event notification?
demand.note: No saved page gives a detection time or a notification time for infrastructure-layer (layer 3/4) events. Looked in www/shield/faqs ('How quickly are events mitigated?' answers only for application layer events), ddos-event-detection (no timing), ddos-standard-summary, ddos-automatic-app-layer-response ('within seconds rather than minutes' for the Anti-DDoS rule group).

demand.question: How do AWS WAF L7 DDoS protection (Anti-DDoS managed rule group) and Shield Advanced relate: can the WAF feature be bought without Shield Advanced, and do Shield Advanced customers pay extra?
Hypothesis: AWS Shield network security director (preview 2025-06-17) became 'AWS Network Security Manager', GA 2026-09-24 in us-east-1. Label it not examinable yet; what does it do in one line?
demand.note: No saved page says that AWS Network Security Manager is a renamed AWS Shield network security director. The GA post (2026-09-24) does not mention network security director; the WAF guide still documents network security director as a preview. Both labelled not examinable.

demand.question: When is Shield Advanced worth buying, according to AWS (ddos-advanced-summary-deciding), and why did Callvale decide not to buy it at stage 3?
What is AWS Firewall Manager: central configuration and management of firewall rules across the accounts and applications of an organization?

What are the prerequisites of Firewall Manager (AWS Organizations with all features, a Firewall Manager administrator account, AWS Config enabled, AWS RAM for Network Firewall and DNS Firewall policies)?

Which policy types does Firewall Manager manage (AWS WAF, Shield Advanced, security groups: common, content audit, usage audit; network ACLs; Network Firewall; Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall; third-party firewalls)?
Does Firewall Manager apply a policy automatically to new accounts and new resources in scope, and can you run a policy without automatic remediation (audit only)?
How is policy scope set (include or exclude accounts and OUs, resource types, resource tags)?
Is a Firewall Manager policy Regional? How do you cover several Regions, and how is a CloudFront (global) WAF policy handled?

How does a Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy manage web ACLs in member accounts (first and last rule groups set centrally, account owners add rules in between; can retrofit existing web ACLs since 2024-10)?
What does Firewall Manager cost (per policy per Region per month, plus AWS Config and protected-service charges), and is it included with Shield Advanced?
Firewall Manager quotas (policies per organization per Region, accounts in scope, administrators).
Can there be more than one Firewall Manager administrator account (multiple administrators since 2023-04), and what can each administer?
How do you see compliance of a policy, and where do findings go (AWS Security Hub)?
What do Firewall Manager security group policies do (common: apply a security group to accounts; content audit: check rules; usage audit: remove unused or redundant groups)?
Hypothesis: Firewall Manager added network ACL policies on 2024-04-25/29. Confirm and state what they enforce.
What does a Firewall Manager Shield Advanced policy do (adds protection to in-scope resources in every account; can enable automatic application layer mitigation)?
What does a Firewall Manager Network Firewall policy create in member VPCs (firewall subnets, endpoints, route tables), and what does a DNS Firewall policy do?
What is AWS Network Firewall: a stateful, managed network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for VPCs?
Which traffic can Network Firewall filter (to and from an internet gateway, NAT gateway, VPN, Direct Connect, between VPCs through Transit Gateway)?
How is it deployed: a firewall endpoint in a dedicated firewall subnet in each Availability Zone, and VPC route tables send traffic to the endpoint?
Why must traffic of one Availability Zone use the firewall endpoint of the same AZ in both directions (asymmetric routing breaks stateful inspection)?
Where does the firewall sit in the internet gateway plus NAT gateway pattern (route from the NAT gateway subnet to the firewall endpoint, then to the IGW)?
demand.note: arch-igw-ngw shows the NAT gateway pattern only as a diagram; the asymmetric-routing sentence about the NAT gateway subnet sits after a bold label and fails M4. Use network-firewall-route-igw-both-directions and network-firewall-no-asymmetric-routing.

demand.question: What are the stateless and stateful rules engines, and in which order does a packet meet them (stateless first; pass, drop or forward to stateful)?

How does a domain list rule group allow only approved outside domains (HTTP Host header and TLS SNI inspection; allowlist or denylist), and does it need TLS decryption?
Strict rule order versus action order for stateful rules, and which default actions exist under strict order (drop established, drop all, alert)?
What does TLS inspection do (decrypt, inspect, re-encrypt; inbound and outbound), and which certificates does it need (ACM)?
Geographic IP filtering (2024-08) and URL / domain category filtering (2026-01): what can each rule match?
Which AWS managed rule groups exist for Network Firewall (domain and IP lists, threat signatures, active threat defense), and is active threat defense on by default now (2025-11)?
demand.note: adjudicate-08 (2026-10-12): the rule group kinds are grounded. network-firewall-atd-default-alert-mode-console was rejected: the current guide shows 'Enable Active Threat Defense - optional' and no saved page confirms the alert-mode default after the 2026-08-10 console change. One line each: AWS WAF vs Shield Standard vs Shield Advanced vs Network Firewall vs Firewall Manager (layer 7 rules vs DDoS vs VPC traffic inspection vs central policy). Use the decision guides' own words.
